newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: UGANDA'S MUSEVENI PROMOTES AFRICAN CAPITALISM.
newsitem.headline: UGANDA'S MUSEVENI PROMOTES AFRICAN CAPITALISM.

text.p: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni made a strong call on Tuesday for the development of African capitalism to help the continent compete in the global marketplace.
In an address to the Cape Town parliament, Museveni urged South Africa to cooperate with its African neighbours to promote growth and begin to close the wealth gap with the rest of the world.
"Use South Africa's unique position to engage in partnership with the rest of Africa in the form of investment, trade and tourism," he said.
Museveni said a capitalist approach to development would help Africa catch up with fast-growing regions such as South East Asia.
"It is the capitalist who brought discipline into production with the balance sheet.... capitalism has made a revolutionary contribution to the struggle for greater production," he said.
Echoing South African President Nelson Mandela's regular call for an African renaissance, Museveni said the 1990s should be seen as the decade of Africa's awakening.
But he said Africa could compete against countries the size of the United States or China and blocs like the European Union only if it formed its own cross-border alliances.

He urged South Africa to encourage harmonisation between the Southern African Development Community (SADC) and the Community for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa), southern Africa's rival trade blocs.
"Now that African economies are beginning to grow, basing themselves on private enterprise, we must think of one additional factor - the size of the market," he said.
